title: weighted-prefetch-and-heartbeat-strategy
content:
Purpose

Working notes for a lightweight multi-region steering primitive intended to reduce cold-handsoffs, respect latency SLOs, and avoid cascading failovers by combining: (1) weighted prefetch/warm pool strategies per-region, (2) heartbeat-gated failover with adjustable cooldown and decay, and (3) small control-plane APIs for temporary weight nudges. Goal: a pragmatic approach we can roll into the routing control plane (steering controller) without requiring wholesale changes to DNS or global Anycast behavior.

Context and motivation
- Problem: sudden regional ejection (uber-dns/infra incident, noisy neighbor on a GPU cluster) causing immediate client re-resolution and global flapping. When clients re-resolve they often shift to a secondary region that is cold (no KV cache, no warmed model shards) which increases latencies and amplifies load to the secondary, sometimes causing it to degrade and cascade.
- Observed in cluster experiments: 20–35% p95 latency spike on initial re-route events; 40% higher token cost due to cold-decoding passes and cache misses.
- We need a middle ground between blunt-region-ejection and immediate global Anycast failover. Aim for graceful local fallback with short-lived pre-warm and a control-plane weight ramp.

Principles
1) Make the client-facing handoff window smaller and more predictable (latency budget).
2) Ensure backend readiness (prefix/KV cache warm, model shard readiness) before shifting a large fraction of traffic.
3) Keep the control-plane simple: weight nudges + TTL-aware DNS hints + heartbeat gating.
4) Fail fast on clear regional outage, but decay routing weights slowly to avoid oscillation.

Key concepts- Weighted prefetch: temporarily bias routing weights toward target regions before actual traffic shift; used to prime warm pools.
- Warm pools/prefetch workers: ephemeral pre-warm connections that replay a small set of cached prompts (synthesized from production prompt sketches) to populate KV caches and GPU scheduler queues.
- Heartbeat gating: nodes/regions emit health heartbeat slices (latency/p95, queue-depth, token-throughput). The steering controller only performs weight shifts when a minimal heartbeat stability window has been satisfied.
- Weight decay & cooldown: after an ejection or reroute, weights decay over a configurable half-life to avoid immediate reversion.

Control-plane API sketch- POST /steering/v1/weight-nudge  body: { region: string, delta_weight: float, ttl_seconds: int, reason: string, prefetch: boolean }
- GET /steering/v1/region-status/{region}  returns last_heartbeat_ts, p95_latency_ms, queue_depth, sim_warm_pct
- POST /steering/v1/prefetch/start  body: { region: string, model: string, preset: string, target_concurrency: int }
(These are shown for reminder — real API will be smaller.)

Operational flow (happy path)
1) Probe detects a reliability degradation in region A: p95 > configured threshold OR control-plane ejection requested.
2) Controller marks region A "degraded" and calculates candidate distribution: nudge small fraction x% of traffic to N region(s) B/C for warm-up.
3) Controller issues weight-nudge to DNS/steering policy with prefetch=true and ttl_seconds=60.
4) Prefetch workers in B/C start reheating caches for model versions seen in the last 24h using a lightweight replay set (~1% of normal qps).
5) After warmpool readiness and 2 heartbeats stability, controller issues final weight shift (larger delta) and increases TTL to stable value.
6) Monitor latency and errors; if p95 grows in new region, rollback using a rapid weight-adjust with short TTL.

Edge cases and failure modes
- Cache-consistency: client session affinity with KV cache across regions is impossible for some workloads; we should detect heavy KV-dependent sessions and prefer session pinning rather than steering.
- Model-variant mismatch: prefetch must respect the exact model + quantization profile in serving. Use model fingerprinting to avoid warming wrong binary.
- Backpressure amplification: prefetching too aggressively can saturate a regional buffer and worsen tail latency. Limit prefetch to a small fraction and rely on queue_depth signals.
- DNS TTL jitter / client resolvers: many resolvers honor low TTLs poorly; the scheme must be robust to resolver caching by being incremental and not assuming instant global change.

Metrics to track (pair with dashboard)
- handoff_p95_increase_pct: percent increase in p95 during handoff window.
- warmpool_ready_ratio: fraction of warm workers that achieved cache targets within target latency.
- prefetch_cost_delta: estimated additional token/GPU cost during prefetch window.
- failover_backoff_events: count of rapid rollback / re-tries per week.
- session-affinity-violations: measured mismatches for KV-heavy sessions.

Experiment plan (A/B)
- A: baseline (immediate weight flip / existing ejection behavior).
- B: weighted-prefetch with pre-warm and heartbeat gating.
- Duration: run 2 weeks, target 1M handoff attempts split across customers.
- Success criteria: 20% reduction in handoff_p95_increase_pct AND no more than 10% increase in prefetch_cost_delta.

Concrete config knobs (defaults to tune)
- prefetch_target_pct = 5  # percent of normal qps used for pre-warming
- prefetch_ttl = 60  # seconds to keep initial small TTL for clients/resolvers
- heartbeat_window = 3  # number of consecutive heartbeat slices required
- weight_nudge_step = 0.05  # 5% weight shifts per nudge
- cooldown_half_life = 300  # seconds for weight decay
- max_prefetch_concurrency = 50

Example steering policy snippet (pseudo-yaml)
---
policy: regional-steering
predicates:
  - name: latency_outage
    threshold_ms: 800
actions:
  - type: mark_degraded
  - type: weight_nudge
    params:
      target_regions: [eu-west-1, eu-central-1]
      step: 0.05
      prefetch: true
      ttl_seconds: 60
      lock_window_seconds: 180

Open decisions
- Should warmpool be co-located with dedicated hot nodes (separate instance class) or run on existing serving fleet with lower priority? Tradeoffs: cost vs isolation.
- Prefetch prompts: use sampled real prompts, synthetic prompts, or deterministic canonical prompts per model? Privacy concerns with replaying customer prompts — default to synthetic/canonical unless explicit opt-in.
- How long to treat a region as "recovering" before returning weights to normal? (current proposal: cooldown_half_life * 3).

Action items
- [Aisha] prototype prefetech worker that can run small replay sets and report sim_warm_pct by 2025-01-24.
- [Ravi] add instrumentation for warmpool_ready_ratio and handoff_p95_increase_pct to per-route dashboards by 2025-01-30.
- [Marina] legal/privacy check on prompt replay and synthetic prompt generation by 2025-02-07.
- [Samir] simulate the policy in steering-sim with a workload trace from Dec 2024 by 2025-01-21.

Notes from sim run 2025-01-18 (quick findings)
- With prefetch_target_pct=5 and heartbeat_window=3 we saw median handoff p95 reduction ~27% on synthetic replay traces.
- Prefetch cost increased ~6% in the simulated window.
- Aggressive prefetch (>=15%) started to push queue depth in warm targets and increased variance.

Related docs and references
- refer: multi-region-handling-guidelines (internal Confluence)
- refer: steering-sim README and trace library

Loose long-term ideas (brainstorm)
- Cross-region cache gossip: a lightweight invalidation/gossip channel for prefix-level hot state (very tricky for correctness).
- Client-assisted hints: optional client SDK header to request session-pinning or to indicate tolerance for cold-handsoff.
- Edge-side prewarming using CDN workers for very latency-sensitive prefixes.

This doc is intentionally informal — use as a sketch for the steering RFC. Will follow up with a more concrete control-plane API and a simulation notebook once Samir's runs finish.
